questions.stem: A student has two unlabelled bottles, one containing hexane and the other hex-1-ene. Which test would distinguish between them?

options.text: Add water — the alkene will dissolve but the alkane will not
Add bromine water — it will decolourise with the alkene but remain orange with the alkane
Smell them — alkenes have a sweet smell while alkanes are odourless
Heat them — only the alkane will burn

questions.explanation: Bromine water is the standard test to distinguish alkenes from alkanes. Alkenes contain a C=C double bond that reacts with bromine in an addition reaction, decolourising the orange bromine water. Alkanes have no double bond and do not react with bromine water at room temperature, so the solution stays orange.

questions.stem: The general formula for alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ. An alkene has 6 carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula and how many hydrogen atoms does it contain?

options.text: C₆H₁₄ — 14 hydrogen atoms
C₆H₆ — 6 hydrogen atoms
C₆H₁₂ — 12 hydrogen atoms
C₆H₁₀ — 10 hydrogen atoms

questions.explanation: Using the general formula CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes: when n = 6, the number of hydrogen atoms is 2 × 6 = 12, giving C₆H₁₂ (hexene). Note this is 2 fewer hydrogens than the corresponding alkane (hexane, C₆H₁₄) because the double bond means two fewer hydrogen atoms can be accommodated.

questions.stem: Ethene (C₂H₄) is described as an unsaturated hydrocarbon, while ethane (C₂H₆) is saturated. Why does this make ethene more reactive?

options.text: Ethene has fewer hydrogen atoms so it is less stable
The C=C double bond in ethene can open up to form new bonds with other atoms in addition reactions
Ethene is a gas while ethane is a liquid
Ethene has stronger intermolecular forces

questions.explanation: The C=C double bond is the functional group of alkenes and is the site of reactivity. One of the two bonds in the double bond can break open, allowing each carbon to form a new bond with another atom or group. This is called an addition reaction. Alkanes lack this double bond, so they cannot undergo addition reactions.

questions.stem: Ethene burns with a smokier, more yellow flame than ethane. What causes this difference?

options.text: Ethene contains oxygen atoms that produce the yellow colour
Ethene has a higher carbon-to-hydrogen ratio, making complete combustion less likely and producing more soot
Ethene burns at a lower temperature than ethane
Ethane produces more carbon dioxide than ethene

questions.explanation: Ethene (C₂H₄) has a higher proportion of carbon relative to hydrogen compared to ethane (C₂H₆). This means more oxygen is needed per molecule for complete combustion. In air, complete combustion is less likely, leading to incomplete combustion that produces carbon particles (soot), which glow yellow in the flame.

questions.stem: The first member of the alkene series is ethene (C₂H₄), not methene (CH₂). Why can there be no alkene with only one carbon atom?

options.text: Methene exists but is too unstable to study
A double bond requires two carbon atoms, so the minimum is C₂H₄
Single carbon atoms cannot form any bonds
Methene is actually the same as methane

questions.explanation: Alkenes are defined by having a C=C double bond. A double bond must exist between two carbon atoms, so at least two carbons are required. With only one carbon atom, it is impossible to form a carbon-carbon double bond. This is why the simplest alkene is ethene (CH₂=CH₂) with two carbon atoms.
